featured_reviews.name: Pankaj
featured_reviews.review_text: High-quality Indian food served at the Taj Lands End in Bandra. Went on a Thursday evening with family for a small celebration. The restaurant has a very old school decor, and the menu is also classical Indian without the unwanted flashes of modern-Indian or gastronomy. As a group of 8, we started with some beverages before settling down on some much needed food through the appetizers. We ordered the Tandoori brocoli,  paneer tikka, mutton, and chicken kababs. All the appetizers were filling and well cooked and satiated our hungry stomachs perfectly well. For mains, we ordered a variety of food again, including the methi machli, sunday mutton curry, paneer lahori, lasooni palak, dal tadka and boondi raita with an assortment of Indian breads. The mains were filling and well cooked. The standout was the fish and the paneer. It was but natural that we would want to end the meal on a sweet note and choose to share the kulfi and the angoori rabri. The desserts were delicious and a perfect end to a fulfilling meal. Considering the restaurant is in a 5 star hotel, prices were just as fancy with the average price of a dish around INR 2000-3000. Service was prompt and courteous.

featured_reviews.name: Pranay Anthwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
hi,

Had a disaster of an experience at Masala Bay yesterday.

but...
First off let me say I'm a huge Tata Group fan. Huge is an understatement. Love their philosophy and how they look after their employees too. Doggys too.

Am also a huge Taj Landsend fan for 20+ years.

My colleague & now friend was down from Singapore for a few days and we had to catchup and also do a business kind of chat so we decided Taj Landsend as a meetup place. I suggested that. and I asked a person who I like and respect who works there - where do we eat, we would like a buffet/indian continental. He suggested Masala Bay, the best for Indian food.

When we met up at 2 pm, we went there.

We ordered
starters
- Prawns Lasunia (was not good. the taste was so so, probably for international palate but we couldn't easily even cut the prawns piece with fork/knife)

- chicken angari (again strictly ok, average, but better than prawns, imagine)

main course was a bigger disaster
- Roomali roti (for some reason they put oil/butter inside Roomali, that's another type of prep only and i hate Roomali like that)
- dhabewala chicken (I can't tell u how horrible this was. I think they put sauce in it and the chicken pieces were terribly cooked, no marination nothing)
- We grumbled a little
- Service was very attentive and everyone including manager was concerned but what could they do.
- then they suggested dhaniya murgh, i req spicy so chef put so much lal mirch with oil on top that even that was terrible.
- they could make out we were leaving food and not very happy
- so they got the chef out.
- I didn't speak w the chef becos it was so bad I would have said something that would have just hurt him.
- the gratis pan at the end was good.
- we quietly paid the bill and left.

- we went down to the lobby and I just had water where as my friend to change the taste of the mouth had to resort to Gin/tonic.

I would seriously recommend either get new chefs or do something. This was not just terrible as per Taj standards but also terrible as per even a dingy small hole in the wall restaurant standards.

Then realising ur paying 8500 for it is criminal.

hope other foodies read this and stay away, don't burn their experience and money.

featured_reviews.review_text: Service was good as well as the food. Ordered the lamb curry, butter chicken, chicken tandoori and some sweet desert. We had a late dinner around 11pm and the restaurant was still quite busy even for a Sunday night

featured_reviews.review_text: We recently stayed at the Taj and had the pleasure of dining at Masala Bay. The service/hospitality and most of all the food was outstanding, to say the least. Everything was on point, from presentation to taste to quantity. Masala Bay did not fail to disappoint.

featured_reviews.review_text:

featured_reviews.name: Piyush Aggarwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
As a long-time patron of Taj Lands End, I was disappointed by our recent lunch at Masala Bay. What was intended as a premium business catch-up resulted in a sub-par meal that did not reflect Taj’s usual excellence.

The Critique:
• Starters: The Prawns Lasunia were tough and difficult to cut, while the Chicken Angari lacked any distinct character.
• Mains: The Dhabewala Chicken felt uninspired—poorly marinated with a sauce-heavy base—and the Dhaniya Murgh was overcompensated with spice and oil rather than balanced flavor.
• Value: At a price point of ₹8,500, the culinary execution felt significantly below industry standards.

The Silver Lining:
The service staff and management were exceptionally attentive and clearly concerned by our feedback. While the hospitality remains world-class, the kitchen requires immediate attention to its consistency and flavor profiles. We left feeling the meal was unfortunately "criminal" for the price paid.

featured_reviews.name: Raj doesn't share food
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Veranda around 4 PM, and the first thing to note is that the kitchen was partially closed at that time, which limited a few options. Still, we managed to order a decent variety of dishes.
We tried prawns thecha, chicken 65, chicken tenders, pizza, pasta, and Hakka noodles. Most of the food was actually good and enjoyable. The highlight of the meal was definitely the prawns thecha, easily the best dish on the table. It was flavorful, well-cooked, and something I’d genuinely go back for.
The pizza and pasta were nice, chicken 65 was solid, and overall the food quality was pretty satisfying. But the Hakka noodles were a letdown. They had a strong smell, likely from the egg and chicken, which made it hard to enjoy the dish.
Another downside was the timing of the chicken tenders. They arrived way too late, almost after we were done eating everything else, which kind of ruined the flow of the meal.
That said, the ambience is where Veranda really stands out. The place looks amazing, has a great vibe, and the location is perfect for a chill outing in Bandra.
Overall, it’s a good place with great ambience and mostly good food, but a few issues with timing and consistency in dishes hold it back slightly.

featured_reviews.name: Ashok Sankaran
featured_reviews.review_text: This tiny cafe on Waterfield Road is perfect for dinner with you and your family. The cozy setting, featuring pale green and pink decorations, gives you that perfect peaceful atmosphere. Earth Cafe offers a variety of options whether you’re vegetarian, Jain or just wanting something different. The food is high quality with something for everyone. The avocado bruschetta has the perfect amount of crispness and flavour. The fries are freshly made, perfect for a crunchy starter. The peach and mint mojito is to die for. To choose a main dish is nearly impossible. From freshly baked sourdough pizzas or piping hot risotto. The lasagna is an amazing dish with layered zucchini and a creamy vegan sauce. If you’re not already stuffed and want a sweet treat, they have a variety of cakes to choose from including some gluten free options. But the perfect treat for summer is the mango and cream. The service was exceptional and the staff were super helpful. Overall an amazing place to dine out. Rahul who served us during our visit was great.

featured_reviews.name: Riddhiman Chanda
featured_reviews.review_text:
Linking Road in Bandra is home to some of the best food in the city, and one of the best asian joints in the place is The fatty Bao. It has a modern, chic vibe crossed with a vibrant and sassy decor, perfect for a date night, or for a hangout sesh with friends.

The decor feels inspired by Malay/Singaporean cafes, with a lot of the artwork depicting the same, and it comes off pretty well. They have both indoor and outdoor seating, though the indoor seating is a bit cramped, but that's mostly fine. They do have a small bar serving the usual suspects, as well as some of their own stuff.

While I didn't get to order a large chunk of their menu, whatever I had was pretty great. Their name is definitely apt, as the baos I got were plump and pillowy, and the filling was perfect. I got the pork char siu baos, and the pork was fatty and melt in your mouth, complimented nicely by a slice of raw apple, giving it a fruity kick. Every Bao order comes with two, making it perfect for date night.

I also got their raw papaya salad, which was one of the best renditions of the dish I've eaten in Mumbai. It was tangy, sweet and spicy in just the right amounts, and wasn't just a refreshing palate cleanser, but a great meal by itself. It's also a very generous portion making it great for sharing.

The last thing I got were Chicken and asparagus dumplings, which didn't impress me as much, as I've had better dumplings in the same price range. They weren't bad but not particularly great either. The filling was generous, but it lacked in flavor. For 6 pieces, it was not the best value, and I recommend trying other dumplings, or avoiding dumplings all together.

Overall, I would rate both the Char Siu Bao and the Papaya Salad a solid 9/10, and the dumplings about a 6.5/10. Definitely go for their baos( pretty obvious given their name).

The service was fine, but they do tend to ignore the smaller tables and focus on the bigger groups, and it was also pretty busy on the day I visited. But I did see other tables also not receiving food at the proper times, so I'd rate the service a little lower, like a 6/10. Definitely could do with some improvement.

The Fatty Bao definitely ticks a lot of the boxes, though they do miss a little bit in their service, and cocktail variety, though I did not have the opportunity to try it. However, they more than make up for it with their snazzy decor and contemporary vibe, along with some pretty great food. I highly recommend checking the place out if you're out shopping in Linking Road and need to grab some lunch or dinner. You're definitely gonna be leaving a happy and fatty bao when you're done.

Final rating- 8.5/10, definitely recommend.

But this consisted just of rice, noodles and sautéd veggies. There were no manchurian balls nor there was any gravy which adds to the taste in sizzlers. REALLY A BIG WASTE OF MONEY, I WOULDN'T RECOMMEND YOU TO ORDER ANY SIZZLER AFTER TRYING THIS ONE AS THIS WAS OVERPRICED AS COMPARED TO ANY OTHER PLACE.

It came across as dismissive, and at times borderline rude. This is what prompted me to finally write this.

name: Love in Langos
description:
Langos is a typical Hungarian food. Nowadays it is a deep fried flatbread, but in the past it was made of the last bits of the bread-dough and baked at the front of a brick or clay oven, to be served hot as the breakfast of the bread-baking day.
Up to the mid 20th century, bread was baked once a week due to the cost of heating up the large oven and the lengthy proces. Because the bread loaf, typical to Hungary, was 6 to 10 pounds each, traditionally they used to bake smaller (1-2 pounds) "cipó" rolls for the evening and the next day. The name lángos (literally meaning "flamed") comes from baking these flat breads.

Love in Lagos - Cafe serves both baked and Fried versions. Lets try some.

featured_reviews.review_text:
I hae been a regular at EAC since 2019. It has been my go-to for years, and while it remains a staple in my Bandra circuit, have noticed some shifts lately that are hard to ignore.
The freshness of their ingredients is honestly amazing - you can taste the quality in every bite. Over the years, I have tried almost everything on the menu across all sections, except for their new bread menu and the salads.
​The Food Journey
​When it comes to the food, I have had nearly all their desserts. If they have the Opera Pastry, it is a absolute must-try. On the other hand, the Tiramisu was just average. If you're going for a drink, the Pineapple Coriander Cooler and the Spiced Mojito are my absolute favorites, but the Vietnamese Cold Coffee is extremely bad - a hard skip.
For mains, their Chicken Burgers, especially the Peri Peri and Grilled Chicken, are top-notch. The Paneer Roasted Veggie Sandwich is also amazing. If you are there for breakfast, the Eggs Benedict is definitely the highlight.
​Pro Tip: You have to try their Roast Chicken with Mashed Potatoes; it is easily their most famous and iconic dish. Hard skip - anything fish.
However, lately, I have noticed the quality seems to have taken a dip. It is not a massive drop, but they have been increasing their SKUs (adding more items), and it is hard not to notice that the consistency isn't what it used to be.
The seating layout here is easily the best of any cafe in Bandra, but a recent experience with the crowd has made me think about stopping my visits completely.
​We were sitting near a table that was loud - uncomfortably loud. A man accompanied by two ladies spent hours shouting. It started with "India vs. Pakistan" and how "we will decimate them," then moved to "India vs. USA" and how the USA is so much better. It turned ugly when he started shitting on Hinduism, calling it a "pagan religion" and preaching Christianity. He kept saying India is "poor, filthy, and bad" because of Hindus and that people should go to churches to "get civilized."
It was highly uncomfortable and left us feeling genuinely shook. I took three weeks to think about whether I should even post this, but the experience was that bad.

Time to hunt for a new go to place.

Visited National near Bandra station 2 days ago. If you’re expecting a fancy ambience or modern cafe type setup, this is not that kind of place. But if you want really good North Indian food at a budget price, this place is definitely worth trying.

The setup is very basic with non AC seating and shared wooden benches. Has that old school fast moving Mumbai food spot vibe. The place gets crowded, especially during lunch and dinner time, but service is quick.

One thing I liked is that they still cook food on traditional coal stoves, so you get that smoky flavour in the food which actually makes a difference.

I tried paneer burji along with roti, Mirchi Laccha Paratha and butter naan. Taste was really good overall and all these were suggested by a guy outside who said veg items are famous there. Price is honestly one of the best parts. A proper meal for two can be done within around 300 to 500 easily.

Overall, simple place, great taste and very budget friendly.

I ordered an Arrabbiata pasta and asked them to replace mushroom with another vegetable. That’s it. Not extra toppings, not some complicated off-menu request — just replacing one vegetable.

And honestly, calling that a “special customization” is ridiculous. It’s pasta, not a five-course tasting menu. Also, I have genuinely never seen mushroom in an Arrabbiata pasta on any normal menu, so acting like removing it was some massive inconvenience was bizarre from the start.

The pasta arrived completely dry, non-palatable, and barely edible, so I gave it 2 stars on the app. I didn’t even write a review initially. But apparently that was enough to trigger the owner into calling me at 11 PM to argue about why I gave a low rating.

The entire call was just constant interruption, defensiveness, and repeated lectures about how they had gone “out of their way” for me by replacing one vegetable with another. If that is considered some massive favour, then maybe don’t offer it at all.

What’s worse is the complete inability to take feedback. If you ask a customer what went wrong, at least let them speak instead of interrupting them every few seconds.

In the restaurant business, bad food is still fixable. This kind of behaviour is what actually ruins the experience. Calling customers late at night to fight over a rating is genuinely bizarre and unbelievably unprofessional.

Definitely not ordering again.

featured_reviews.name: Noor Sayeed Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries in Bandra has such a gorgeous, welcoming vibe, it’s easily one of the prettiest spots for South Indian food in the city. The staff was genuinely sweet and the service was so smooth it made the whole experience feel really relaxed.

We decided to try their new chaat menu, and the Shakkarkand Matar ki Chaat was a total winner, it felt super fresh and not at all oily. The Chatpata Singhada (water chestnut) was a fun surprise too, especially for that unique crunch you don't usually find in street food.

The Madras Diaries Special Combo is a solid choice if you’re like me and can't decide the medu vada was perfectly crispy. But honestly, the real highlight was the Filter Coffee with those Rawa Biscuits. It’s such a nostalgic, comforting pairing. We finished with the Elaneer Payasum, which was light and refreshing, though I wish there was just a bit more of it! Definitely worth a visit if you’re in Bandra and want a meal that feels both clean and satisfying.

featured_reviews.name: Allen Samuel
featured_reviews.review_text:
Madras Diaries is a perfect blend of authentic South Indian comfort and exciting new flavours! The highlight now is their chaat menu, which adds a fun, chatpata twist alongside their classic offerings.

The Chatpata Singhada and Shakkarkand Matar Ki Chaat were vibrant, tangy, and full of flavour. The Chettinad Paneer with flaky wheat parotta was rich and satisfying, paired beautifully with the soft Kodumai (wheat) parotta. Refreshing sips like the Cold Coffee and Virgin Mojito balanced the meal, while the Elaneer Payasam was a light, delicious finish.

The presentation of each dish was impressive and clearly made with attention to detail. Service was warm and prompt, making the overall experience even more enjoyable.

With its warm décor and relaxed, inviting ambience, Madras Diaries is a must-visit for a wholesome meal with a unique chaat twist!

featured_reviews.name: Aaniket R Naddkarni
featured_reviews.review_text:
VARUGA VARUGA ❤️

Everyone is craving South Indian food these days… looks like Idli & Dosa have officially become Gen Z’s favorite comfort food 😍
So we decided to check out Madras Diaries in Bandra — a place already famous for authentic South Indian food, but now they’ve also launched CHATS… and trust me, this will make you visit again & again!

Without wasting any time, we started with our favorite — Pani Puri 🤤
And bhai sahab… they served it with 3 different flavor waters — Mumbai style, Delhiwala & Kolkata style!
We literally couldn’t stop eating 😅

Then came the Palak Patta Chaat…
And bhai, ekdum Delhi ki yaad dila di ❤️

To beat the summer heat, we tried their Kokum Cooler & Mint Cooler — super refreshing and fresh!

For mains, we ordered Mini Idlies served with 4 different chutneys… and trust me, this combo is something you’ll only get here, so make sure it’s on your order list ✔️

We also tried the Malabar Paratha with Chettinad Paneer — great quantity, rich flavors, and the paneer was super soft 😍

And finally in desserts, Pineapple Sheera… simple, comforting, and honestly made with love ❤️
So make sure you visit Madras Diaries

featured_reviews.name: Yash Rungta
featured_reviews.review_text:
A recent vegan lunch at Rare Earth Cafe turned out to be a genuinely delightful surprise.

Coming from a vegetarian family but someone who enjoys meat and seafood outside, I’ve always felt that the real advantage of being non-vegetarian is the freedom to eat anything—vegan, Jain, or otherwise. This place reinforces that idea beautifully.

Their cashew cheese is truly top-notch. It’s different from dairy cheese, but in a way that feels like an upgrade rather than a compromise. Everything tastes thoughtfully crafted. The flours they use—millets or emmer wheat—are light and easy to digest, which you can actually feel after the meal.

And the dessert? Easily a 7-star experience.

What stands out is their commitment to making everything in-house, using natural ingredients as much as possible. It shows in every bite.

You don’t need to be vegan to enjoy this place. Whether you’re vegetarian, non-vegetarian, eggetarian, Jain, or vegan—this café is absolutely worth a visit.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
We’ve been regular visitors to Donna Deli and have always appreciated the good food and prompt service earlier. That consistency is what made us keep coming back.

However, over our last two visits, the experience has not been the same. The food quality didn’t match what we were used to, and the service took much longer than expected, with a wait time of over 30 minutes. There also appeared to be some lack of coordination between the order-taking and the kitchen, which led to part of our order being missed.

The staff were courteous and seemed to be doing their best, so this is not a complaint about their attitude or effort. It felt more like operational gaps that need attention.

It’s disappointing to see a place we genuinely like going through this phase, and we truly hope the management addresses these concerns and restores Donna Deli to its earlier standard.

featured_reviews.name: SGT Reviews
featured_reviews.review_text:
SGT Reviews | Sip • Grab • Taste ⭐

Donna Deli – Bandra West | Saturday Dinner Review

📍 Location & First Impressions
Donna Deli sits right on SV Road, Bandra, a short stroll from Khar Road Station so if you’re planning to drive, God be with you. If you're walking in, the white-washed European façade welcomes you like you’ve entered a Pinterest board.
Pro Tip: If it’s a weekend, reservation is non-negotiable. This place fills up quicker than your WhatsApp family group on Diwali morning.

🍽️ What We Tried

1. Truffle Pizza

Creamy, crispy, indulgent basically everything you want from a pizza that wears truffle like a crown. If royalty had a flavor, this would be it.

2. Truffle Fries

Yes, more truffle. Don’t judge.
We inhaled these while waiting for our drinks. Perfectly crisp, generously tossed, and honestly… finished too soon.

3. Donna’s Signature Drinks

We tried a bunch of their mocktails (let’s just say the menu has more Donnas than a Bollywood family tree). Refreshing, quirky, and worth experimenting with.

4. Hungover Noodles (⭐ The Star of the Night)

Do not go by the looks.
These noodles pack flavour, comfort, and a bit of drama. Easily the winner and something you’ll crave again.

🛎️ Service

Shockingly fast.
I mean the food arrived before our mocktails.
They take the “fast” in fast-casual seriously.

🌿 Ambience & Vibe

Donna Deli scores big here white décor, leafy corners, soft lighting, aesthetic touches everywhere. Instagram would approve. So would your date.

🚗 Parking & Access

Located right on SV Road

Walking distance from Khar station (recommended)

If coming by car, patience is a mandatory side dish

📌 Final Verdict – SGT Meter

Ambience: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
Service: ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

South Indian food isn't all idlis and dosas and I'm happy to see a few restaurants such as The Tanjore Tiffin Room that's here to prove this point.

The Jackfruit Cutlet and Sweet Potato Yellow Chilli are great appetizers. I prefer the cutlet more owing to the interesting tangy chutney that's served with it.

We were planning to directly order the main course but our server suggested that we first sample their offerings in the form of a tasting platter. Definitely go for the tasting platter which is provided to you at no cost - it's a beautiful presentation.

It was only after the tasting platter that we opted to go for the Vegetable Madras Railway Curry. The tomato and cream base paired so well with the Malabar Parotta.

Our server recommended the Lemongrass Cooler and it was a refreshing choice.

While our experience, the food, and the service were great, what surprised me was a South Indian restaurant whose Sambar was so average. That being said, multiple visits to The Tanjore Tiffin Room are in my future.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text:
The Tanjore Tiffin Room is one of the finest places in the city to enjoy authentic South Indian cuisine in a refined yet welcoming setting. From the moment you enter, the ambience sets the tone — warm, classy, and thoughtfully designed with a blend of traditional and contemporary elements. It strikes the perfect balance between being vibrant and cosy, making it ideal for both family meals and relaxed dining with friends.

The food is truly the star here. Every dish is crafted with rich, traditional flavours that reflect the culinary heritage of South India. The tasting platter is a must-try, offering a wonderful selection of signature items that allow you to sample a variety of dishes in one go. Whether it’s the dosas, curries, or starters, everything is cooked to perfection and beautifully presented. The flavours are authentic without being overly spicy, appealing to a wide range of palates.

The service is excellent, with staff who are attentive, polite, and well-informed about the menu. Their recommendations are spot-on, and they ensure you’re comfortable throughout your visit. Another convenience is the availability of valet parking, which makes dining here hassle-free, especially during busy hours.

Overall, The Tanjore Tiffin Room delivers a delightful South Indian dining experience with great food, superb service, and charming ambience. Highly recommended.

featured_reviews.name: Sunil Kamat
featured_reviews.review_text:
Good stuff indeed ! The famous Madras Railway curry (mandatory) and Ghee Roast were both good ! The Mutton cutlets were awesome ! Only thing I found out of form was the Kokam Sour punch drink - weirdly
sour !!

featured_reviews.name: Vidhi S
featured_reviews.review_text:
Grateful for friends who recommend great dishes! The Madras Railway Curry with appams is one of the most comforting meals I’ve had. Would 10/10 recommend.

Notable mentions: Vegetable Stew & Khorma. Bonus: Lemongrass Cooler

featured_reviews.name: Nive Raitz von Frentz
featured_reviews.review_text:
Prettily lit entrance leading a climb of a couple of floors to the restaurant (there is a lift). At 7:30 pm, several tables were already occupied.

Nicely presented menus, friendly staff, delicious home style recipes served in chunky brass dishes, complementary colours and textures.

Small tasting bowls of curry and rice samples are a prelude to the main course. The food is heavy, so go easy on the ordering!

We had hardly finished our starters, when the main courses piled up on the table...service could be staggered slightly.

Loos are off a small landing and could be cleaner. On our way out, the entrance area had become jammed with waiting guests, a tight situation, as were the takeaway boxes, which were over-stuffed.

featured_reviews.name: Daniel Harrington
featured_reviews.review_text:
Absolutely stunning in every way.

Fell across this place via Google maps and waited until 10pm for a table (our fault we didn't book), however it did not disappoint.

Genuinely a top 5 all time restaurant for me. The food, the service, the ambience absolutely top tier. I have never had Indian food (from any region) as flavourful. The staff explained the concept and dishes incredibly well and the taster platter to help decide what to order was so fantastic. I would recommend this to absolutely everyone who lives in or is visiting Mumbai.

Thanks for an unforgettable night.

Please open up in London!!

featured_reviews.review_text: Good food and nice ambiance, service was rather slow but we appreciated the thought put into the curry tasting platter and the detailed description for each curry dish. Really happy with the meal 🥘

The decor of the place gives such authentic vibes, you feel like visiting the whole of Punjab in that cute small space.

featured_reviews.name: Ramsha Tausalkar
featured_reviews.review_text: There’s a spot in Bandra that serves North Indian food so good, you’ll forget that you’re in Mumbai and be transported straight to Punjab. It’s called Papa Pancho Da Dhaba and they’ve got a menu that’s small and straightforward - but they do these dishes so well and in such an authentic manner - we for sure haven’t had such North Indian food in Mumbai. The Dal Makhani, Cheese Kulcha, Makhani Chicken, Kasturi Kebab, Dahi Papdi Chaat and Matka Kulfi - all of your seemingly regular dishes but here it’s all elevated, rich and very real. The interiors are colourful and very dhaba-like. If this is a cuisine you enjoy, save this spot!

featured_reviews.name: Pulastya Dave
featured_reviews.review_text:
Excellent experience for a family get together had yesterday for lunch.
Ordered the following:
Papa Pancho Special Chicken Tikka
Mutton Seekh Kebabs
Mutton chaap
Mutton bhuna
Chicken biryani
Dal tadka
Jeera Rice
Butter Garlic Naan
Sarson ka saag with Makkai Roti
Everything was excellent, but the mutton dishes were truly amazing as such fine quality of the meat is rarely experienced at restaurants in general, so I highly recommend ordering mutton dishes here.
Staff is polite and friendly & service is relatively quick.
I will certainly return to try more dishes in the future.

featured_reviews.name: Nikshay Gupta
featured_reviews.review_text: Great spot for North Indian food in Mumbai. We mostly ordered vegetarian dishes, and the Sarson da Saag with Makke di Roti was honestly so good. The service was a bit slow, but totally worth the wait.

featured_reviews.review_text:

food:

featured_reviews.name: Dr. Kartik Patil
featured_reviews.review_text:
Papa Pancho da dhaba is a kind of experience amidst the by-lanes of hype Bandra Pali Hill. You get into this colourful world of roadside dhabas as soon as you step in. Sparkly danglers, colourful patakas, slogans written on trucks decorated on the walls.
Food:
Good, guilty and gluttonous North Indian food is served with love on brass cutlery. You feel the butter in every bite. Quality is great, though quantity is frequently insufficient for a couple of people. Earlier they used to include dal makhani and dahi etc. with their mouthwatering kulchas and parathas but now they have stopped doing that. Tandoori Starters and tandoor breads are must try for.
Service: servers are frank and friendly and a bit too nosy sometimes.
Ambience: small place, but they made max out of it. They transfer you to dhaba instantly.
Value for money: This would disappoint you, as for what they ask for; their quantity is too little. Hope they work on their quantity.
A highly recommended place for small group or family to visit if you are craving some good Kulchas, Parathas, Tandooris and a glass full of lassi.

I’ve tried so many things from Papa Pencho butter chicken, dal, chole bhature, kulche, dahi papdi chaat and not a single thing has ever disappointed me. Everything is consistently so good, which is honestly rare.

But if there’s one thing you have to try, it’s the Papa Pencho’s Tikka my absolute favourite. I literally beg you to order it. It’s that good.

featured_reviews.name: Rivha Dalvi
featured_reviews.review_text:
Imagine a dhaba in the middle of the city and that too in Bandra!! Well got an opportunity to visit “ Papa Pancho da Dhaba” with family. Was surprised on a Thursday night, it was crowded with people waiting to be seated, that is how popular the place is.

We ordered the Tandoori Chicken which was crisp from outside and moist from inside, well spiced and really tasty.  Next was Dahi Pappi Chat, a well balanced crispy, chatpata, khatta meetha, but for the cost, the quantity could be a lil more.

In main course it was Chicken Handi with Butter Garlic Naan, served with Dal Makhni and Curd. Next was but for sure Amritsari Kulcha…. served with white butter dollop and buttery dal makhni. We were almost full, but on suggestion we ordered Chicken Dal Khichadi, which surprisingly was very comforting with bits of Chicken … we ended the meal with  Lassi… a must at any Punjabi place. A huge copper glass full!!

Stumbled upon The Lovefools in Bandra with my partner — and honestly, what a find! It’s literally a hidden, handpicked gem tucked away in the cutest little corner. ✨

We went all out with the food — Malabar Sukka, Dal Baati Tart, Asparagus Kulcha, Yaki Pork Chashu, and Belper Knolle Chicken — and not one missed the mark. Every dish was bursting with flavour and beautifully done.

The drinks? 10/10.
We had the Shirley, a refreshing watermelon + Stranger & Sons gin cocktail (so damn good), and Leo, which is a vodka cocktail, chocolatey, vermouth-y, and totally indulgent. 🍸

Personally, the best part was the place itself. The ambience is truly amazing - dim lit, cozy, lots of romantic lights.

Big shoutout to Yash, our waiter — super sweet, attentive, and made the experience even better.

It’s definitely on the pricier side (around ₹800+ per dish), but honestly, so worth it for the vibe, the food, and the overall experience. Can’t wait to go back!

featured_reviews.name: Prithvish Ashar
featured_reviews.review_text:
@thelovefools

The Lovefools on Hill Road, Bandra West, is a gem that feels like stepping into a dreamy Goan bungalow.

Chef Sarita Pareira has an amazing menu and the place  offers a warm, vintage vibe with pastel rooms and chandeliers, perfect for a cozy date or family meal.

The menu is a fun mix of Italian, Japanese, Asian, and Indian flavors, making every bite exciting.

Their “Lunchish” menu, launched in 2025, is a slow, soulful treat with dishes like the Jay Fai Bucket List—a crab omelette with Kerala curry—and Sawadee Mango Toast, blending mango with spicy Thai salad. The Gambas Al Ajillo, prawns in chili oil, is a must-try for its bold taste. However the Dinner Menu and Vibe is completely different.

The fully stocked bar serves creative cocktails like Shirley and Chimbai, celebrating Bandra’s local vibes. Service , is friendly and attentive.

Check out their IPs , Wednesday is their gig , packed place.

Brie Brioche was the star dish , so was the Lemon malay curry , do try the signature and the most selling dish Umami twist and Andhra Vada
Their desserts are worth a try.

Over all this place is a gem
Will be back soon
Kudos to the team
Till we meet again , cheers

#vintage #goan #vibe #gigs #blogger
featured_reviews.response_from_owner_text: Thank you for sharing such an enthusiastic review! We're thrilled to hear that you enjoyed the warm atmosphere and our diverse menu, especially the standout dishes like Brie Brioche and Umami Twist. It's wonderful to know that you appreciated the creative cocktails and attentive service as well. We can't wait to welcome you back for more delightful experiences and live gigs. Cheers to more memorable moments at The Lovefools!

featured_reviews.name: Susmita Hegde
featured_reviews.review_text: I had a fantastic lunch at Hakkasan—the food and service were top-notch. Dhananjay gave us excellent service.We started with the Spicy Chicken Dumplings (a must-try—super flavorful and spicy; we had them twice). Next came the tender Stir Fry Chicken. The Peach Passion drink was perfectly tangy. We finished with the 5 Style Stir Rice with Chilli Combo, packed with great textures and flavors.Hakkasan nails fine Cantonese dining. Highly recommend!

featured_reviews.name: Chirag Patel
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently revisited this upscale Chinese restaurant for brunch, despite previous underwhelming experiences. Unfortunately, the lack of natural light and overuse of tacky blue lights remained a major turnoff. The ambiance, while appealing to some, doesn’t  resonate with me.
The food, while reasonably priced during brunch, didn't change my opinion about Chinese cuisine in Bombay. It still feels like a generic Chinese restaurant in a five-star hotel.

On a positive note, the staff was attentive and well-trained, with noticeably more staff members on deck. The addition of a smoking cabin upstairs was convenient, and the toned-down music was a welcome change. The unlimited flow of good brand cocktails was a great value.

While this restaurant still isn't my favorite, I appreciate the positive changes in price, smoking area, and music volume.

featured_reviews.name: Josef Schneider
featured_reviews.review_text: So glad I booked Hakkasan for my birthday dinner. The food was amazing, especially the Peking duck. The service was friendly and attentive, and I appreciated the excellent recommendations. I'll definitely be coming back here for special occasions.
